title: Man shot and killed by Hamilton Police
article: Ontario's police watchdog is investigating why Hamilton officers fatally shot a man after he was found wandering a busy highway Friday.
Officers from the Hamilton Police Service were called around 9:30 a.m. about a 45-year-old walking against traffic on the busy Lincon M. Alexander Pkwy. near Upper Wentworth St.
The man was ordered by police to get off the road, which he did, but then fled toward a nearby wooded area with officers following behind.
"An ensuing interaction" took place and the man "sustained multiple gunshot wounds" as a result, the Special Investigations Unit said in a statement.
He was pronounced dead at the scene.
Two officers are being investigated, said SIU spokesman Monica Hudon.

The SIU, a civilian law enforcement agency that conducts criminal investigations into incidents involving police and civilians that result in serious injury, death or sex assault allegations, has assigned nine investigators to look into the deadly shooting.
Hudon wouldn't comment on what "interaction" took place between the man and police, nor did she say if he brandished a weapon of any kind.
Hudon couldn't say why the man was walking on the road and that determining if drugs, alcohol or mental illness was a factor is part of the SIU's investigation.
Hudon said the investigation is ongoing and that it would be "irresponsible" to give further specifics.

The Hamilton Police Service was the subject of nine complaint letters from the SIU involving incidents between 2008 and 2011. The complaints sited concerns around officers' note-taking, failure to notify the SIU, officer conduct, and officers' refusal to answer questions about their notes.

The complaints drew the attention of Ontario's ombudsman in 2012, who said Hamilton Police responded in a substantial way to only three of those nine letters, and that much improvement was needed in the relationship between Ontario's police and the SIU.
